descriptors.R: the sitting President, nominee of the party that has held the White House since 2017
descriptors.D: nominee of the party that has held a majority in the House of Representatives since the 2018 elections; a former Vice President

compile_desc.R: the party that has held the White House since 2017
compile_desc.D: the party that has held a majority in the House of Representatives since the 2018 elections

others_line: Other candidates on most ballots, including a Libertarian and a Green nominee (answer "other").
never_name: Trump, Biden, Pence, Harris, Obama, Clinton, Sanders, Warren, Buttigieg, Jorgensen, Hawkins or Pelosi

slice_sources.men: 2019 and 2021 American Community Survey (1-year, IPUMS; the 2020 1-year release is experimental only) interpolated to November 2020; men who are citizens 18+ (the native_white, naturalized, black and other slots) less those barred for a felony conviction (Sentencing Project / Uggen et al. state estimates for 2020); outside the eleven former Confederate states; turnout and choice calibrated to the certified 2020 returns.
slice_sources.women: 2019 and 2021 American Community Survey (1-year, IPUMS; the 2020 1-year release is experimental only) interpolated to November 2020; women who are citizens 18+ (the native_white, naturalized, black and other slots) less those barred for a felony conviction (Sentencing Project / Uggen et al. state estimates for 2020); outside the eleven former Confederate states; turnout and choice calibrated to the certified 2020 returns.
slice_sources.south-white: 2019 and 2021 American Community Survey (1-year, IPUMS; the 2020 1-year release is experimental only) interpolated to November 2020; white non-Hispanic adults in the eleven former Confederate states (US-born in the native_white slot; white naturalized citizens sit in the naturalized slot), less felony disenfranchisement (Sentencing Project / Uggen et al. state estimates for 2020); calibrated to the certified 2020 returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 2019 and 2021 American Community Survey (1-year, IPUMS; the 2020 1-year release is experimental only) interpolated to November 2020; US-born Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states, all citizens with no legal bar beyond felony disenfranchisement (Sentencing Project / Uggen et al. state estimates for 2020), which falls on them disproportionately; calibrated to the certified 2020 returns.
slice_sources.immigrants: 2019 and 2021 American Community Survey (1-year, IPUMS; the 2020 1-year release is experimental only) interpolated to November 2020; noncitizen adults (the alien slot), who cannot vote in federal elections; naturalized citizens are counted in the naturalized slot and can vote.

masks: the nominee of the party out of the White House
